abstract: Maintains polar satellite uplink and emergency telemetry response records
system_message:
You are Communications and telemetry systems lead (TEL). The communications and telemetry systems lead (TEL) maintains polar satellite uplink and emergency telemetry response records, as well as auxiliary renewable power telemetry across traverse routes.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains polar satellite uplink and emergency telemetry response records（SAT）
information_points.content:
TEL-SAT-6VL：For the Queen Maud Plateau Northern Transect, satellite distress telemetry is enabled on the autonomous package aboard the lead tractor sled, and its emergency telemetry broadcast latency across latitudes 75°S to 82°S reaches a maximum of 12 min.
TEL-SAT-N4P：For the Wohlthat Mountains Crest Route, satellite distress telemetry is enabled on the autonomous package aboard the lead tractor sled, with an emergency telemetry broadcast latency reaching a maximum of 25 min across latitudes 75°S to 82°S.
TEL-SAT-GEN：For the Princess Astrid Coast Ascent Corridor, satellite distress telemetry is enabled on the autonomous package aboard the lead tractor sled, and the emergency telemetry broadcast latency measured across latitudes 75°S to 82°S is 8 min.

information_points.title: Auxiliary renewable power（SOLAR）
information_points.content:
TEL-SOLAR-JCK：For the Princess Astrid Coast Ascent Corridor, the sled-mounted solar photovoltaic array provides an auxiliary solar output of 450 W peak power yield under clear polar summer insolation.
TEL-SOLAR-SJH：For the Queen Maud Plateau Northern Transect, the sled-mounted solar photovoltaic array provides an auxiliary solar output of 600 W peak power yield under clear polar summer insolation.
TEL-SOLAR-TAH：For the Wohlthat Mountains Crest Route, the sled-mounted solar photovoltaic array provides an auxiliary solar output of 300 W peak power yield under clear polar summer insolation.
